subject: Can Unmarked run single-season models with heterogeneous detection probabilities (finite mixtures)?

messages.author: eff863edad129425
messages.subject: Can Unmarked run single-season models with heterogeneous detection probabilities (finite mixtures)?
parts:
Hello,

I have a quick question on whether Unmarked can run single-season models with heterogeneous detection probabilities (finite mixtures) as described in MacKenzie et al 2006 Chapter 5.1? I'm conducting a study on mapping seagrass distribution using a range of biophysical/environmental covariates in turbid shallow water and would like to compare this model with the standard single season model as I suspect that differences in seagrass cover is causing heterogeneous detection probabilities. I'm aware that Program Presence is able to do this but see many advantages of using Unmarked in the R Program.

Thank you.

Tony Griffiths

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Can Unmarked run single-season models with heterogeneous detection probabilities (finite mixtures)?
parts:
Dear Tony,

no, it cannot. It can, however, fit the Royle-Nichols model, which is another way of accommodating detection heterogeneity.

Kind regards  --  Marc
